### Areas Not Covered

All four Python checklists were loaded before reviewing the diff. Checked normalization, empty-string compatibility, caller behavior, test coverage, security, architecture, and removal candidates. No actionable regression was substantiated.

The parent reports all four tests passed on Python 3.10.12, six boundary cases passed through both `build_payload` and `save`, and the staged whitespace check was clean. I did not execute tests under this read-only role.

`display_name.strip()` requires an input supporting `.strip()`. Neither documentation nor existing tests establish support for `None` or numeric inputs, so their changed behavior does not substantiate a regression finding. Python 3.9 was not exercised.

Both Capy lookups returned an empty knowledge base. No live `/settings` service contract or deployment configuration is available. The evidence supports code approval and local correctness for the tested string inputs; production deployment readiness remains unverified.
